description: Binary vs Continuous D-study budget comparison
data_source: probit simulation TRUE_VC (continuous) + observed Henderson I (binary) + simulation oracle (binary, p=0.7)

formula.sigma2_delta: sum(sigma2_{k x item} / n_k) + sigma2_residual / prod(n_k)

continuous.source: probit simulation TRUE_VC (latent continuous, 1296-condition matched design)

binary_oracle.source: probit simulation oracle (p=0.7, 10000 items, matched 1296-condition design)
binary_oracle.note: Fair within-simulation comparison with continuous TRUE_VC

primary.description: Continuous TRUE_VC vs Observed Binary (cross-source comparison)
primary.interpretation: The continuous latent scale (TRUE_VC) requires 80% more items than the observed binary data to reach G>=0.80. This is driven by the TRUE_VC's higher delta/tau ratio (0.124 vs 0.068): the simulation was designed with proportionally larger facet x item interactions relative to item_id than the real data exhibits. This comparison conflates the effect of binarization with the mismatch between simulation and observed variance structure.

within_simulation.description: Continuous TRUE_VC vs Binary Oracle (fair within-simulation comparison)
within_simulation.interpretation: Within the same simulation, binarization increases the D-study budget by 36.4%. Binarization inflates residual (16% -> 41%) and compresses item_id (50% -> 32.1%), worsening the delta/tau ratio from 0.124 to 0.168. This is the expected direction: Bernoulli noise degrades per-item reliability, requiring more items to achieve the same G threshold.

comparison.key_finding: The within-simulation comparison (fair) shows binarization costs +36% items. The observed binary data has a more favorable variance structure than the simulation predicts (delta/tau = 0.068 vs 0.124), so its D-study budget (55 items) is lower than both simulation conditions.
